headline_marked: [[GTA 6]] car theft gets complex, requires tools & specific methods
headline: GTA 6 car theft gets complex, requires tools & specific methods
summary: Rockstar is adding layers of stratification to vehicles, meaning hotwiring every car won't be possible. Some will require specific tools or methods to steal.
details: Grand Theft Auto VI will feature more complex car theft mechanics, moving beyond the simple 'hotwire and drive' of previous titles. Rockstar aims to make vehicle acquisition more meaningful and varied.
According to Rockstar's Rob Nelson, players will need to acquire specific tools and progress further in the story to access certain parked cars. However, carjacking drivers will remain an option.

Vehicles with electronic key fobs may require a key cloner, while those with GPS systems might necessitate driving at a certain speed to avoid detection. An in-game app will reportedly help players identify necessary tools and a car's value.
These changes are part of a broader effort to add depth to gameplay and decision-making for players. The goal is to make the cars players drive feel more significant within the game's world.

Despite these gameplay previews, GTA 6 continues to be plagued by leaks. A hacker known as 'Cyberleek' has been releasing clips of the game, a situation Rockstar has described as 'heartbreaking' as they investigate the source.
caption:
Stealing cars in GTA 6 won't be as simple as pressing a button anymore. Get ready for more complex mechanics and required tools.

Grand Theft Auto VI will feature more complex car theft mechanics, moving beyond the simple 'hotwire and drive' of previous titles. Rockstar aims to make vehicle acquisition more meaningful and varied.

According to Rockstar's Rob Nelson, players will need to acquire specific tools and progress further in the story to access certain parked cars. However, carjacking drivers will remain an option.

Vehicles with electronic key fobs may require a key cloner, while those with GPS systems might necessitate driving at a certain speed to avoid detection. An in-game app will reportedly help players identify necessary tools and a car's value.

These changes are part of a broader effort to add depth to gameplay and decision-making for players. The goal is to make the cars players drive feel more significant within the game's world.

Despite these gameplay previews, GTA 6 continues to be plagued by leaks. A hacker known as 'Cyberleek' has been releasing clips of the game, a situation Rockstar has described as 'heartbreaking' as they investigate the source.
